1  THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MV ACT,
 PRAYING TO ALLOW THE APPEAL BY MODIFYING THE  -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-K:542  MFA No. 200119 of 2023 JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 17-02-2022 IN MVC NO.607/2017, PASSED BY THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND ADDL. MACT AT BASAVAKALYAN AND CONSEQUENTLY BE PLEASED TO ENHANCE THE COMPENSATION OF RS.4,91,520/-
WITH INTEREST @ 12% PER ANNUM FROM THE DATE OF PETITION TILL ACTUAL REALIZATION.
 THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This Appeal is filed by the claimant aggrieved by the judgment and award passed in MVC No.607/2017 dated 17.02.2022, the claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of the compensation.

The claim petition was filed seeking compensation of an amount of Rs.8,00,000/-
for the injuries sustained by the claimant in the accident.
2. It is the case of the claimant that he was working as a labourer and earning an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month.

As per the evidence of the doctor, the claimant had sustained 56%
disability.

The Court below had considered the income at Rs.6,000/- per month, and the disability at 1/3rd of 56% as 18% disability and granted the compensation under the following heads:
NC: 2024:KHC-K:542 Heads Compensation Amount 1.

For pain shock and mental agony : Rs. Rs.10,000/-
2.

For permanent disablement : Rs. Rs.1,68,480/-
3.
For medical expenses incurred : Rs. Rs.1,00,000/-
4. Further medical expenses : Rs. Rs.20,000/-
5 . Nourishment and attendant : Rs. Rs.10,000/-

Total Amount of Compensation : Rs. Rs.3,08,480/-
3.
Learned counsel for the appellant submits that claimant had sustained four grievous injuries.
Under the head of pain and suffering only an amount of Rs.10,000/- is awarded.

It is submitted that for the injury sustained by him when he was in hospital for 32 days, the Court had granted only Rs.10,000/- under the head of nourishment and attendant.
No amount is granted under the head of loss of amenities.
He submits that even for the loss of earning during laid up period no amount is granted.

It is NC:
2024:KHC-K:542 submitted that the compensation that was awarded by the Tribunal is not just and reasonable.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the insurance company submits that the Court below had rightly granted the compensation basing on the evidence.
He submits that the doctor in the disability certificate has stated about the disability to the limb, which is assessed at 56%.

In view of the same,
it has to be 1/3rd and Court below had rightly taken 18%.
He submits that under all the heads the compensation that was awarded is just and reasonable and no grounds are made for enhancement of the compensation.
5. Having heard the learned counsels on either side, perused the material on record.

In this case,
according to the claimant, he was earning an amount of Rs.10,000/- per month by working as a coolie.
The accident has taken place in the year 2017.
As per the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the year 2017 the income shall be taken as NC: 2024:KHC-K:542 Rs.10,250/-.
As the claimant had stated that he was earning Rs.10,000/-, this Court is considering the income at Rs.10,000/-.
Then coming to the disability as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the respondent, this Court has perused the disability certificate.
The doctor considering the injury had given 56% disability to the limb.
The Court had rightly taken 18% (i.e.1/3rd).
under the head of loss of future income, he is entitled for an amount of Rs.2,80,800/-.

Then under the head of pain and suffering, as per the wound certificate the claimant had sustained four grievous injuries and this Court is granting an amount of Rs.80,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
Towards Medical expenses and future medical expenses, Court below had rightly granted compensation basing on the evidence on record and no interference is called for.
Then coming to the loss of earning during the laid up period, as this Court has taken Rs.10,000/- as income for three months he is entitled for an amount of Rs.30,000/-.
Considering four NC: 2024:KHC-K:542 grievous injuries and impact on the future happiness, an amount of Rs.30,000/- is granted under the head of loss of amenities.

6. In the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of V.MEKALA vs. M.
MALATHI AND ANOTHER1, the claimant is entitled for an amount of Rs.10,000/- towards legal expenses.

(a) The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition, till the date of realization.

Hence, the claimant is not entitled for interest for the period 91 days delay in filing the appeal.
(c) Respondent-Insurance Company shall deposit the said compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within a period of 8 (Eight) weeks.
(d) The Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Record to the Tribunal along with the certified copy of NC: 2024:KHC-K:542 the order passed by this court forthwith without any delay.
